text:
maria_cs: Heads-up: AtlasAI reported a billing spike after an SSE reconnect. They received 3 near-identical completions for the same prompt after a network blip. Customer says each completion was billed. Repro steps below.

tom_eng: Can you paste the exact client flow + headers and any server logs you have? Is the client resuming with seq or resume_token?

maria_cs: Repro from customer (copied):
```
# client behavior
1) open SSE GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-infer&session=abc
2) network disconnect (short)
3) client sees last_event_id=950 and immediately reconnects:
   GET /v1/stream?session=abc&resume_token=rt_abc&last_seq=950
# headers they sent
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx
Idempotency-Key: (not set)
```
Server logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-12T10:02:05Z] connection closed session=abc
[2026-03-12T10:02:06Z] resume request session=abc last_seq=950 -> accepted (resume_snapshot=960)
[2026-03-12T10:02:06Z] runtime: generate gen_id=g-111 seq=951..955 -> emitted
[2026-03-12T10:02:06Z] runtime: replay from snapshot seq=951..955 -> emitted (duplicate payloads seen by client)
```
Customer: saw 3 complete outputs, all billed.

jess_support: We've issued provisional refunds for the duplicated usage and opened an escalation. Need eng to confirm root cause and a short-term mitigation.

tom_eng: From logs it looks like resume was accepted and resume_snapshot is ahead of client's last_seq. Two things could happen: either we replay cached outputs from snapshot OR we recompute new outputs. We should not do both. Do we have any request_id attached to the generation to detect duplicates?

vikram_sre: Check ingest/journal to see whether we wrote multiple generation records or if the client re-sent the same request. If there's no request_id on the client side (as maria said), server-side dedupe is required.

ingest-bot: journal lookup for session=abc:
```
last_ack=950 last_seq=960 snapshot_epoch=3 resume_token=rt_abc
no request_id present on incoming resume
generated records: g-111 @10:02:06, g-112 @10:02:07
```

tom_eng: Interesting — journal shows two distinct gen_ids (g-111 and g-112). That implies the runtime BOTH replayed cached output and also produced a fresh generation, or it retried generation while replaying. Hypothesis: resume handshake is not atomic; a replay task and a recompute task can race and both push chunks to the SSE connection.

vikram_sre: Agree. Short-term mitigation options:
- enable strict-resume-mode for the customer (server rejects resume if client last_seq < resume_snapshot by N)
- treat resume acceptance as an atomic action: either deliver cached events OR start recompute, not both
- add idempotency check server-side by attaching gen_id/request_id and dropping duplicates at delivery layer

jess_support: I can flip strict-resume-mode for AtlasAI now. I'll tell billing to track any further anomalies and hold off on additional refunds until we confirm. Customer wants a clear explanation.

tom_eng: For the long-term fix I'm going to implement the handshake change: when resume request arrives, runtime will lock session state, determine whether the snapshot covers client's last_seq; if snapshot covers it, replay-only path; else, recompute-only path. Also add an explicit resume_nonce in token so stale tokens can't be accepted after a snapshot advance. Will add unit tests around concurrent resume+recompute.

vikram_sre: Immediate canary plan: deploy runtime patch to canary nodes with a feature flag, monitor per-session duplicate generation metric and post-deploy billing delta. I'll correlate with journal writes. :eyes:

maria_cs: Customer accepted the temporary setting. Thanks for the quick turnaround. Please include steps for CS to explain the root cause: short statement: "a rare race between resume replay and regeneration caused duplicate outputs; we refunded duplicates and enabled stricter resume validation while we roll out a fix."

tom_eng: I'll open PR and link the unit test + rollout notes. Patch will also add a defensive dedupe in the delivery layer to drop duplicate gen_ids if seen twice in a short window. Rollback plan: toggle feature flag off if we see regression.

jess_support: I'll follow up with customer once patch is on canary and after we confirm reconciliation. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
